summary: Control-plane mirroring in private VPC causing opaque 429s after cross-region control-plane sync
description:
Issue summary: After enabling the experimental control-plane 'mirroring' sync for NovaHealth's private VPC control plane (intended to mirror control-plane events to a standby region), they observed opaque 429 throttling on production API requests. Impact: Customer reports widespread 429s across mixed realtime/chat and bulk embedding routes for ~90 minutes during the sync window; user-facing latency and request failures for critical clinical ingestion pipelines. Environmental notes: Private deployment (self-hosted control plane) behind our private API gateway image; control-plane mirroring was enabled via flag: CP_MIRROR_SYNC=true. Mirroring streams pass through the customer's VPC peering path and an internal HAProxy layer that rewrites headers. Observed behavior: 5–15% of requests return 429 with no X-RateLimit-* headers visible to the customer; server-side rate-limiter logs show tokens being consumed twice for a subset of incoming requests when mirrored control-plane traffic is present. Expected behavior: Mirrored control-plane events should not cause duplicate accounting against tenant token buckets or per-route burst pools.

Temporary customer impact/workaround: Support recommended temporarily disabling CP_MIRROR_SYNC on the private control plane while SRE investigates. This restored normal traffic for the customer within 10 minutes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On a private control plane deployment with CP_MIRROR_SYNC enabled, configure mirror target to a standby region.
2) Route production API traffic through customer's HAProxy layer configured to preserve X-Client-ID and X-Forwarded-For.
3) Trigger a small-scale model rollout to warm the standby region (causes short burst of control-plane events).
4) Observe 429s on mixed chat/embed routes and check server rate-limiter accounting.
investigation_notes: 03/11 03:00 - Initial triage: customer saw opaque 429s with no throttle headers; suspected token accounting mismatch.
03/11 03:20 - Correlated 429 spike with control-plane mirroring start; control-plane emitted duplicate route-update events for a 15s window.

03/11 03:40 - Captured VPC flow logs and ingress HAProxy logs: mirrored events were re-injected to API path with preserved X-Client-ID, resulting in duplicate token accounting by the token-bucket service.

03/11 04:10 - Reproduced locally in staging by enabling mirroring and a simple header-preserving proxy; confirmed token_delta recorded twice for the same request-id when mirror replay occurred within same refill epoch.

03/11 05:00 - Hypothesis: control-plane mirror replay + header-preserving proxy leads to identical client-id + request signature being accounted twice because the dedupe layer relies on origin-request-id which is not preserved across mirror flow.
comments: 2026-03-11 03:15 - NovaHealth (customer): 'We started seeing 429s exactly when we flipped mirroring on. No changes to our app. Requests just started failing.'
2026-03-11 03:50 - Support (Priya): 'We're investigating. Can you confirm if HAProxy rewrites any X-Request-ID or origin headers? Any preserved request-id would help us correlate.'
2026-03-11 04:05 - NovaHealth: 'HAProxy is set to preserve X-Client-ID and X-Request-ID for tracing. We can toggle preservation if needed.'

2026-03-11 04:45 - SRE (Marisol): 'We see double token deltas in the rate-limiter for requests that have mirrored control-plane events within the same epoch. We're testing a fix to dedupe mirrored accounting by checking mirror flag + origin timestamp.'
2026-03-12 09:00 - Support: 'Recommend disabling CP_MIRROR_SYNC temporarily while we push a mitigation to edge-proxy and token-bucket for dedupe. Customer confirmed disabling resolved issue.'
root_cause: Control-plane mirroring caused replayed control events to be re-injected to the API path with preserved client identifiers. The token-bucket accounting pipeline lacked adequate deduplication for mirrored events when origin request IDs were preserved, leading to double-counting against tenant and per-route burst pools.
resolution: Mitigation deployed: quick patch to token-bucket service to detect mirrored-control flag and ignore mirrored replay events for accounting when origin-request-id matches a recently recorded request (10s window). Deployed to staging on 2026-03-11 08:30 and to private deployments as a config patch 2026-03-12 07:15.
Customer action: Disabled CP_MIRROR_SYNC during investigation; re-enabled after patch verification and saw no recurrence during a 2-hour soak in canary region.

Follow-ups: (1) Update control-plane mirroring runbook to include guidance on not preserving origin request ids across mirror replay flows or tagging mirrored events with a unique mirror-origin header. (2) Add a token-bucket test case to simulate mirror replay and ensure dedupe holds across refill epochs. (3) Schedule postmortem with NovaHealth and internal ops team (confluence page link added).
next_steps: 1) Engineering to harden dedupe in token-bucket: extend detection window to 30s and add metrics for mirrored-accounting-suppressed.
2) Documentation: add paragraph to Private deployment checklist about header-preservation and mirror configs.
3) Customer follow-up: schedule a runbook review call with NovaHealth for 2026-03-16.
4) Create an automated integration test that simulates mirrored-control-plane playback and asserts no duplicate accounting.
